title: Island Kitchen Design Ideas for Thai Homes
excerpt: Islands bring prep space, storage and seating into the heart of the home. Here is how to size, place and finish a kitchen island for homes in Thailand.
metaTitle: Island Kitchen Design Ideas Thailand | Thailand Kitchens
metaDescription: Island kitchen design ideas for homes in Thailand: sizing, walkways, seating, sinks and hobs in islands, and finishes that cope with tropical humidity.
sections: Start with the walkways

An island needs clear space on every side so doors open and two people can pass. Measure the room first, then size the island to fit the walkways rather than the other way round. In compact condos, a slim island or a peninsula is often the better choice.
Decide what the island does

Prep, cooking, washing up or socialising: each role changes the design. A sink or hob in the island needs water, drainage, power and ventilation brought through the floor, so decide early, before the floor is finished.
Seating and overhang
Bar seating needs a worktop overhang deep enough for knees, and enough width per stool. Facing the seats towards the living room or garden keeps guests part of the conversation while you cook.
Finishes for a tropical climate
Quartz and sintered stone worktops resist stains and humidity. Moisture-resistant carcasses and sealed edges keep the island stable through the rainy season.
highlightTitle: Plan the island around people, not just cabinets
highlightText: The best islands are sized for how your family moves through the kitchen every day.
quote: An island should invite people in, never block their way.

title: The L-Shaped Kitchen: A Practical Guide for Thai Homes
excerpt: The L-shaped kitchen is one of the most efficient layouts for condos, townhouses and villas. Learn how to plan corners, storage and the work triangle.
metaTitle: L-Shaped Kitchen Guide Thailand | Thailand Kitchens
metaDescription: A practical guide to L-shaped kitchens in Thailand: work triangle, corner storage, breakfast ledges and layouts for condos, townhouses and villas.
sections: Why the L works
Two connected runs create a natural work triangle between sink, hob and fridge while leaving the rest of the room open. It suits corner spaces in condos and open-plan rooms in townhouses and villas.
Solve the corner
The corner is the hardest place to reach. Carousel units, pull-out corner systems or a simple blind-corner drawer turn dead space into usable storage for pots and small appliances.
Add a breakfast ledge
Extending one leg of the L with a slim counter creates a place for coffee or homework without the footprint of an island.
Light both runs
Under-cabinet lighting on both legs prevents shadows where you work. A window on one run brings daylight to the prep area.
highlightTitle: Efficient, flexible and easy to fit
highlightText: The L-shape works in more rooms than any other layout, from compact condos to family villas.
quote: Good kitchens start with good corners.

title: U-Shaped Kitchens: Maximum Storage and Workspace
excerpt: A U-shaped kitchen wraps the cook in storage and worktop. Discover when the U-shape works best and how to keep it open and comfortable.
metaTitle: U-Shaped Kitchen Storage Ideas | Thailand Kitchens
metaDescription: When a U-shaped kitchen works best, how wide it should be, and storage ideas that give Thai homes maximum workspace without feeling enclosed.
sections: Who the U-shape suits
Keen cooks and large families benefit most. Three walls of cabinets give the most storage and the longest continuous worktop of any layout.
Mind the width
The space between the arms must allow two people to work and doors to open. A U that is too narrow feels cramped; too wide and you lose the efficiency.
Keep it open
Use open shelving or glass fronts on one arm, or lower one arm to counter height as a breakfast bar, so the kitchen does not feel boxed in.
Zone the three walls
One wall for preparation, one for cooking and one for washing keeps the kitchen organised and lets more than one person cook comfortably.
highlightText: With the right width, a U-shaped kitchen is the most productive layout for serious cooks.
quote: Everything within reach, nothing in the way.

title: Modular vs Custom Kitchens in Thailand: Which Is Right for You?
excerpt: Modular kitchens are fast and predictable; custom kitchens fit every centimetre. Compare cost, timing, fit and finishes before you choose.
metaTitle: Modular vs Custom Kitchens Thailand | Thailand Kitchens
metaDescription: Modular or custom kitchen? Compare fit, finishes, timing and cost to choose the right kitchen for your condo, townhouse or villa in Thailand.
sections: What modular means
Modular kitchens use standard cabinet sizes combined to fit the room. They are quicker to plan and produce, and work well in rooms with regular dimensions.
What custom means
Custom kitchens are built to the exact size of the room, with fillers kept to a minimum. They suit irregular walls, sloping ceilings, columns and high-end finishes.
Comparing cost and time
Modular systems are usually more predictable in price and delivery. Custom work takes longer to design and build but makes better use of every centimetre.
The best of both
Many projects combine standard modular carcasses with custom fronts, worktops and panels, giving a tailored look with the reliability of a system.
highlightTitle: Choose by room, budget and timeline
highlightText: Regular rooms suit modular kitchens; complex spaces and premium finishes reward custom work.
quote: The right kitchen is the one that fits your home and your life.

title: Kitchen Renovation Checklist for Homes in Thailand
excerpt: From the first measurement to the final handover, use this checklist to plan a kitchen renovation in Thailand without costly surprises.
metaTitle: Kitchen Renovation Checklist Thailand | Thailand Kitchens
metaDescription: A step-by-step kitchen renovation checklist for Thailand: measurements, plumbing and electrics, building rules, materials, appliances and installation.
sections: Before design
Measure the room, photograph every wall and note windows, doors, columns, water and drainage points and sockets. Check condo or village rules for working hours and noisy work.
During design
Agree the layout, then choose appliances, because their sizes shape the cabinets. Select worktop and fronts from samples seen in daylight in your own home.
Before installation
Finish walls, floors and ceilings, and move plumbing and electrics to their final positions. Book lifts, parking and access for delivery day.
Handover
Check every door, drawer and appliance, learn how to care for the worktop, and keep the warranty documents together.
highlightText: Most delays come from late decisions. A clear checklist keeps your renovation on schedule.
quote: A good plan is the cheapest part of any kitchen.

title: Quartz vs Granite Worktops: What Works Best in Thailand?
excerpt: Quartz and granite are the two most popular worktops in Thai kitchens. Compare durability, maintenance, heat resistance and looks.
metaTitle: Quartz vs Granite Worktops Thailand | Thailand Kitchens
metaDescription: Quartz or granite kitchen worktops? Compare stain resistance, heat, sealing, UV and maintenance to choose the best worktop for a home in Thailand.
sections: Quartz
Engineered quartz is non-porous, so it resists stains from curry, oil, coffee and wine without sealing. It comes in consistent colours and suits busy indoor kitchens.
Granite
Granite is natural stone with unique patterns. It handles heat and sunlight well, which makes it a good choice near large windows and for outdoor kitchens. It needs periodic sealing.
Marble and sintered stone
Marble looks luxurious but etches with acids, so it suits low-use areas. Sintered stone is extremely durable and UV-stable, ideal for terraces and sunny kitchens.
How to choose
Indoor family kitchens usually favour quartz; outdoor and sun-exposed kitchens favour granite or sintered stone. See large samples before deciding.
highlightTitle: Match the stone to the space
highlightText: Quartz wins indoors for easy care; granite and sintered stone win in sun and heat.
quote: A worktop is the hardest-working surface in the home.

title: Condo Kitchen Ideas: Making Small Kitchens Work in Bangkok
excerpt: Bangkok condos often have compact kitchens open to the living room. Smart layouts, tall storage and integrated appliances make them work beautifully.
metaTitle: Condo Kitchen Ideas Bangkok | Thailand Kitchens
metaDescription: Small condo kitchen ideas for Bangkok: compact layouts, tall storage, integrated appliances, light finishes and building rules for renovation.
sections: Choose a compact layout
Straight, galley and small L-shaped kitchens make the most of condo floor plans. Keep the sink near the existing drain, as plumbing in condos rarely moves far.
Store vertically
Cabinets to the ceiling, a pull-out pantry and deep drawers add storage without using floor space.
Integrate appliances
Integrated fridges, slim dishwashers and combination microwave ovens keep an open-plan kitchen calm and uncluttered.
Respect building rules
Check working hours, lift bookings and deposit requirements with the juristic office before installation day.
highlightText: With careful planning, a compact condo kitchen can do everything a large one can.
quote: Every centimetre should earn its place.
